subject: History
central_question: Why did Japan, China, Taiwan and South Korea follow different paths to sovereignty, industrialisation, social change and democracy in the modern era?
in_scope_units: East Asian contrasts, historical sources and debates about modernisation.
Japan under the Tokugawa: political order, urbanisation, commerce, literacy and cultural change.
The Meiji Restoration, nation-building, education, military reform and constitutional tension.
Japanese industrialisation, workers, environmental protest, nationalism and everyday life.
Japanese empire, war, defeat, US occupation, democratisation and post-war economic recovery.
China’s encounter with Western imperialism, the Opium Wars and Qing reform.
The 1911 Republic, Sun Yat-sen, May Fourth movement, Guomindang and social change.
The rise of the Communist Party, Mao’s peasant strategy, Long March and victory in 1949.
New Democracy, Great Leap Forward, Cultural Revolution and market reforms after 1978.
Taiwan’s authoritarian development, land reform, economic growth and democratisation.
Korean colonial rule, division, war and dependence.
South Korea’s export-led industrialisation, authoritarian governments, democratisation and the IMF crisis.
Comparison of East Asian paths to modernity, tradition, nationalism, state power and political participation.
banned_topics: Detailed European Renaissance and Reformation, which belong to Changing Cultural Traditions.
European settler colonisation of America and Australia, which belongs to Displacing Indigenous Peoples.
Detailed ancient Chinese or Japanese history beyond the background explicitly used in this chapter.

known_pitfalls.correction: Tokugawa Japan restricted Western contact but remained involved in East Asian trade and received knowledge through Dutch and Chinese links.

known_pitfalls.claim: Meiji modernisation simply copied the West.
known_pitfalls.correction: Japan adopted foreign institutions and technology while reshaping them through imperial loyalty, existing skills and indigenous traditions.

known_pitfalls.claim: China’s modern history was only a conflict between communists and nationalists.
known_pitfalls.correction: It also involved Qing reformers, republican revolutionaries, foreign imperialism, social movements, regional inequality and changing ideas about tradition.

known_pitfalls.claim: Mao’s communist programme was based mainly on urban industrial workers.
known_pitfalls.correction: Mao departed from orthodox Marxist expectations and built the revolution around the peasantry.

known_pitfalls.claim: South Korean economic growth automatically produced democracy.
known_pitfalls.correction: Growth expanded education, urbanisation and political awareness, but democracy resulted from prolonged citizen, student and middle-class movements against authoritarian rule.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Activity 1 to compare Japan’s encounter with Western pressure to the Aztec encounter with Europeans.
Use NCERT Activity 2 to evaluate Nishitani’s definition of modernity and Japan’s attempt to overcome Western modernity.
Use NCERT Activity 3 to assess what the Opium War painting reveals and conceals about coercive trade.
Use NCERT Activity 4 to analyse how shared discrimination connected Buck Clayton with Chinese observers.
Use NCERT Exercises 6–8 to evaluate Japanese industrialisation, Maoist revolution and the relationship between South Korean growth and democratisation.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Exercises: Answer in Brief, Questions 1–5, and Answer in a Short Essay, Questions 6–8.
